# CSRankings

> > A transparent, publication-based ranking system for computer science institutions worldwide, measuring research output through faculty publications at top-tier conferences.

CSRankings provides data-driven rankings of computer science departments based on faculty publications at selective conferences including CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICLR, ICML, AAAI, and IJCAI. The methodology emphasizes transparency and uses publication metrics rather than reputation surveys, offering an alternative to traditional rankings like US News and World Report.

## Key Topics

- Publication-based rankings
- Computer science research metrics
- Faculty research output
- Conference-based evaluation
- CVPR, ICCV, ECCV (Computer Vision)
- ICLR, ICML (Machine Learning)
- AAAI, IJCAI (Artificial Intelligence)
- University rankings methodology
- Academic transparency
- Citation analysis
- CS institutions worldwide
- Research productivity metrics
- Graduate school selection
- Selective conference publications

## Main Rankings

- [CSRankings: Computer Science Rankings](https://csrankings.org/): Interactive ranking system for computer science departments worldwide based on faculty publication counts at top-tier conferences across AI, systems, theory, and interdisciplinary areas

## Understanding the Rankings

- [FAQ - CSRankings: Computer Science Rankings](https://csrankings.org/faq): Comprehensive FAQ explaining CSRankings methodology, publication metrics, conference selection criteria, and how it differs from citation-based and reputation-based ranking systems like US News

## Graduate School Resources

- [Advice for Applying to Grad School in Computer Science](https://csrankings.org/advice.html): Expert guidance from CS faculty on graduate school applications, including how to use rankings effectively, choosing advisors, and evaluating research programs
